path-tools.names.draw-a-line-across-the-.text: Draw a line across the shapes to cut them in two.
path-tools.names.draw-a-line-across-the-.note: Hint for the Knife tool on the drawing canvas. It tells the user to drag a line that crosses the shapes.

path-tools.names.draw-a-longer-cut-line.note: Message when the Knife line was too short to cut anything.

path-tools.names.fits-the-shape-again-wi.text: Fits the shape again with fewer points.
path-tools.names.fits-the-shape-again-wi.note: Tooltip of the Simplify tool, which redraws a shape with fewer points.

path-tools.names.grows-or-shrinks-the-sh.text: Grows or shrinks the shape by the amount you set.
path-tools.names.grows-or-shrinks-the-sh.note: Tooltip of the Offset path tool, which makes a shape larger or smaller all around.

path-tools.names.join.note: Button name of a path tool that connects two open paths into one. A verb. Not the same as Split.

path-tools.names.join-works-on-open-path.text: Join works on open paths. Use Split first to open a closed one.
path-tools.names.join-works-on-open-path.note: Message shown when the Join tool is used on a closed path. Join and Split are the names of two tools.

path-tools.names.joins-the-two-nearest-e.text: Joins the two nearest ends of the selected open paths. With one path selected, it closes it.
path-tools.names.joins-the-two-nearest-e.note: Tooltip of the Join tool. Open paths have two loose ends; closing a path connects its own ends.

path-tools.names.knife.note: Button name of a path tool that cuts shapes along a line the user draws. Like a kitchen knife, used as a tool name.

path-tools.names.nothing-would-be-left-o.text: Nothing would be left of this shape.
path-tools.names.nothing-would-be-left-o.note: Message when the Offset path tool was set to shrink a shape so far that it would vanish.

path-tools.names.offset-path.note: Button name of a path tool that grows or shrinks a shape evenly all around. Not a move.

path-tools.names.outline-stroke.note: Button name of a path tool that turns a line's thickness into a filled shape. Outline is a verb here.

path-tools.names.pick-a-point-between-th.text: Pick a point between the ends to split here.
path-tools.names.pick-a-point-between-th.note: Message for the Split tool when the selected point is an end of the path and cannot be split.

path-tools.names.select-a-closed-shape-o.text: Select a closed shape. Open lines have no area.
path-tools.names.select-a-closed-shape-o.note: Message for the Offset path tool when the selection is an open line instead of a closed shape.

path-tools.names.simplify.note: Button name of a path tool that reduces the number of points of a shape. A verb.

path-tools.names.split.note: Button name of a path tool that cuts a path in two at the selected point. A verb. Not the same as Knife.

path-tools.names.splits-the-path-at-the-.text: Splits the path at the selected point.

path-tools.names.this-shape-has-no-strok.text: This shape has no stroke to outline.
path-tools.names.this-shape-has-no-strok.note: Message for the Outline stroke tool when the shape has no line (stroke) to convert. Stroke is the line around a shape.

path-tools.names.this-shape-has-too-many.text: This shape has too many points for this tool.
path-tools.names.this-shape-has-too-many.note: Message when a path tool refuses a shape because it has more points than the tool can handle.

path-tools.names.this-shape-is-already-a.text: This shape is already as simple as this setting allows.
path-tools.names.this-shape-is-already-a.note: Message for the Simplify tool when the current Detail kept setting removes no further points.

path-tools.names.turns-the-stroke-into-a.text: Turns the stroke into a filled shape you can edit point by point.
path-tools.names.turns-the-stroke-into-a.note: Tooltip of the Outline stroke tool. Stroke is the line around a shape.

path-tools.panel.a-higher-value-drops-mo.text: A higher value drops more points.
path-tools.panel.a-higher-value-drops-mo.note: Help text under the Simplify setting. Drops means removes.

path-tools.panel.amount.note: Label of the number field for how far the Offset path tool grows or shrinks a shape.

path-tools.panel.apply.note: Button that confirms a path tool's preview and changes the shape. A verb.

path-tools.panel.before-now-after-after.text: {before, plural, one {# point} other {# points}} now, {after, plural, one {# point} other {# points}} after
path-tools.panel.before-now-after-after.note: Preview line of a path tool. {before} is the current number of points of the shape. {after} is the number it will have after the tool is applied.

vars.after: The count the text is about.
vars.before: The count the text is about.

path-tools.panel.cancel.note: Button that closes a path tool's panel without changing the shape. A verb.

path-tools.panel.corners.note: Label of the choice for how the corners of an offset shape are drawn: Round or Sharp.

path-tools.panel.detail-kept.note: Label of the Simplify slider. A higher setting keeps more of the original shape's detail.

path-tools.panel.nothing-to-preview-yet.note: Shown in a path tool's panel before a preview can be calculated.

path-tools.panel.positive-grows-the-shap.text: Positive grows the shape, negative shrinks it. From {min} to {max}.
path-tools.panel.positive-grows-the-shap.note: Help text under the Amount field of Offset path. {min} is the lowest allowed number (negative). {max} is the highest allowed number.

vars.max: The value that replaces max in the text.
vars.min: The value that replaces min in the text.

path-tools.panel.round.note: Option for Corners: rounded corners, the opposite of Sharp. An adjective, not a verb.

path-tools.panel.sharp.note: Option for Corners: pointed corners, the opposite of Round.

path-tools.panel.smooth-corners.note: Checkbox label for the Simplify tool: keep the result smooth and curved instead of with sharp corners.

path-tools.panel.working-on-it.note: Shown while a path tool calculates its preview.
